title: A label can wear a box as well as an outline on its letters
goal: A border added to a piece of text draws a line round each letter, which is what you want when words sit over a busy screenshot. There is no way to put a plain box round the label itself any more, and a bordered label is a common thing to want. Give a label both, and make it obvious which one you are getting.
notes: Fallout from outline-leaves-appearance-and-an-effect-s-colour (2026-09-08). A layer ring on a text layer has always been baked into the text raster as a glyph outline (DocumentRenderer, .text case, TextRasterizer.TextOutline). When the Outline row retired, every border on a label became that glyph outline and DocumentRenderer stops calling borderEffects for text, so the box a Border used to draw round a label (added 2026-09-07) is gone. Likely shape: a per-border choice of what it follows, i.e. widen RingShape to include the letters and let the row pick, or a separate setting in the Text section.
acceptance: A label can be given an outline that follows its letters and a box that follows its frame, and both can be on at once
The row says which of the two it is without having to try it
A document saved before this opens with its letter outline unchanged

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Walked the flow as somebody who has just typed a caption over a screenshot. Two shapes were on the table: (a) each Border row says what it follows, letters or box; (b) a separate switch in the Text section, with Border always meaning a box. Chose (a). Reasons: acceptance asks for BOTH at once, and (a) gives that for free since a border is countable, so a fat letter halo and a thin box are two rows with a grip between them; (b) would have to migrate every saved letter outline back out of the Effects list into a text setting, losing the ordering and the count. Photoshop agrees: a Stroke on a text layer follows the glyphs, which is why letters stays the default and nobody's saved file changes. Cut from the idea: no new Text section, no second plus entry, no per-letter position. Kept small: one picker on the row. Also found the Position popup is shown today on a label's border where it means nothing, since a letter outline has no inside or outside, so it hides itself while the row follows the letters.

Second review, on the probe with real captures (Scripts/playtest/label-border-follows-walk.json). What works: a border arrives on the letters exactly as before, the row reads 'Follows Letters', switching it to Box puts a rectangle round the label and brings the Position row with it, and a second border arrives on the letters so both are on at once. What is rough and went into the audit: the grip between a letter border and a box border changes nothing you can see, since a letter outline is baked into the words and a box ring is laid over them afterwards; and the box hugs the words tight because a label's frame is snug, so a roomier bordered label wants padding on a text layer, which is separate work. One thing the walk taught: with the Follows popup on screen a Border row holds three menus, and the two that had no row name of their own would both have answered to 'Border', so Follows carries its own playtest field name.

A label's Border row now asks what the ring follows: Letters, baked round each letter as before, or Box, drawn round the label's frame, and a label can wear one of each at once. Letters stays the default and is what a border saved before today opens as, so no document changes. PhotonzCore/BorderFollows.swift, DocumentRenderer, EffectsListInspector. Verified by Scripts/test.sh green at 4880 (11 new tests, including the pixels for both rings and a saved label opening unchanged) and walked on the probe with real captures: queue/audits/2026-09-08-label-border-follows.json.
